Read Press Release Talk to us Talk to us > Blog Posts Blog Posts | July 14, 2026 Shoppers Don’t Trust What They Can’t See Yaniv Zukerman CMO and Business Development Link copied Retail transparency means giving shoppers clear, real-time visibility into prices, discounts, product information, availability, and basket totals throughout the in-store journey. For grocery retailers, smart shopping carts can turn this transparency into a practical part of the shopping experience, showing shoppers exactly what they’re buying, what promotions are applied, and how much they’re spending before they reach checkout. From Expectation to Reality In our recent white paper, When Online Expectations Enter the Physical Store , we explored how rising digital standards are reshaping what shoppers expect inside the store. One theme stood out above the rest: the demand for transparency. Online, shoppers are used to complete visibility — exact prices, applied discounts, stock availability, and a running continuously updated basket total, all before they commit to a purchase. That level of clarity has reset expectations for the physical store. In store, that same transparency is often missing. Shoppers are left to interpret shelf labels, estimate discounts, and wait until checkout to learn what they’ll actually pay. The most basic question, — “How much am I really spending?”, — often goes unanswered until the very end of the journey. This gap creates uncertainty, and uncertainty directly shapes behavior. Smart shopping carts are a natural response to this gap. By carrying pricing, promotions, and basket totals with the shopper through the aisle, they bring the same real-time clarity shoppers already expect online into the physical store. Shoppers want one thing above all: to know exactly what they’re paying, with clear prices, accurate discounts, and no surprises at checkout. It was the strongest signal in both our previous and latest surveys: clarity and control drive confidence at every step of the journey. At its core, transparency starts with something simple: shoppers want to know exactly what they’re paying. They expect clear prices, accurate discounts, and continuous visibility into their spending, with no surprises at checkout. This was the strongest signal in both our previous and latest surveys — clarity and control drive confidence at every step of the journey. When visibility is limited, trust erodes quickly. Small inconsistencies between shelf price and checkout, unclear promotions, or the inability to track spending in real time all create doubt, as does a lack of visibility into product availability or location. As a result, shoppers become more cautious, limit their purchases, and avoid anything that adds effort or risk. The Commercial Impact of Transparency This uncertainty carries a direct commercial cost. When pricing, discounts, and basket totals are clearly visible throughout the journey, shoppers can make decisions with confidence instead of caution, reducing hesitation at the shelf and removing the need to mentally track spending as they add items. Real-time spend visibility also unlocks budget utilization. Instead of stopping early to avoid uncertainty, shoppers can actively manage their basket, adjusting, adding, or trading up with full awareness of the financial impact. The result is higher conversion, larger baskets, and stronger engagement with promotions. Over time, consistent transparency builds trust in a retailer’s pricing and checkout experience. When shoppers know that what they see is what they’ll pay, they’re more likely to return, explore new products, and engage confidently with the store. Transparency moves beyond a functional capability to become a driver of long-term loyalty and sustained revenue growth. Beyond Price: Other Dimensions of Transparency Transparency starts with price, but it doesn’t end there. Building real trust means ensuring visibility across the full shopping journey. Product availability and location matter, even in supermarkets where items are physically visible. When a product is missing, shoppers are left guessing whether it’s out of stock, misplaced, or simply overlooked. Clear signals around availability, along with guidance to alternatives, reduce friction and prevent abandoned intent. Product information is another critical layer. In categories like health, fresh food, or private label, shoppers increasingly want to understand what they’re buying: ingredients, origin, nutritional value, or suitability for specific needs. Without clear, accessible information, they default to familiar choices or skip the purchase altogether. Checkout transparency reinforces trust at the most sensitive moment of the journey. Shoppers expect to see exactly how prices, discounts, and promotions were applied, with no discrepancies between shelf and final total. Any mismatch, even a small one, creates immediate doubt. (NASDAQ: AZ), a global leader in smart retail technology, today announced a new in-store retail media agreement with Israeli retail chain HaStock, further expanding the companies' ongoing partnership. Under the agreement, AZ received all in-store retail media and advertising rights across HaStock stores in addition to the on-cart retail media rights already granted to AZ. AZ will be able to offer these opportunities to brands and advertisers, including HaStock's existing suppliers, creating additional in-store media inventory that can be commercialized through AZ. The agreement has an initial term of 24 months. The agreement represents another step in AZ's retail media evolution and is designed to help retailers and brands engage shoppers during the physical shopping journey, while creating measurable media opportunities at the point where purchasing decisions are made. The agreement broadens the available media inventory beyond the Company's Smart Carts to additional touchpoints within the store. This creates a more comprehensive in-store media offering, complementing AZ's core Smart Cart-based retail media capabilities. "Retail media is an important growth opportunity for AZ and a natural extension of the infrastructure and shopper engagement we are building inside physical stores," said Gadi Graus, CEO of AZ . "This agreement deepens our partnership with HaStock and gives us additional opportunities to connect brands with shoppers during the in-store journey. Most importantly, it is another concrete step in building and commercializing our retail media business alongside the continued expansion of our connected in-store commerce platform."
